children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a 26% increase in its consolidated net profit for the September quarter to 5,645 crore from 4,468 crore a year earlier, aided by strong loan growth, higher fee income and lower provisions. Net interest margins, however, narrowed as the share of low-cost deposits in its funding mix declined.

On a standalone basis, the private sector lender's net profit rose 29% to 4,212 crore from 3,253 crore in the second quarter of FY26. Net interest income (NII) increased 16% year-on-year to 8,459 crore from 7,311 crore. Net interest margin (NIM), however, contracted 23 basis points to 4.31% from 4.54%, even as the cost of funds fell 18 basis points year-on-year to 4.52%.

The moderation in margins is attributed to significant mobilisation of foreign currency non-resident bank FCNR(B) deposits during the quarter. "This quarter, we mobilised 55,000 crore through FCNR deposits," said Ashok Vaswani, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Bank.

title: Kotak Bank Q2 Net Profit Jumps 26%, NIM Slips
